nv_horseshoe_wall.blurb: A big trad face on the east side of Mount Wilson in Red Rock, spanning the stretch between the Fin and Resolution Arete above the wooded ledges known as Sherwood Forest. All ten climbs here are trad lines, split roughly evenly between the 5.9, 5.10 and 5.11 ranges, and they are long, serious multi-pitch outings that can run to double-digit pitch counts. Most of the effort is the approach: an unmarked bushwhack up Willy's Couloir that takes a couple of hours before the climbing starts. Expect a committing day with a full trad rack, plenty of solitude and no quick escape.

nv_holiday_wall.blurb: A small sandstone sport alcove in the Calico Tanks area of Red Rock Canyon, tucked beside the drainage a short uphill walk along the Calico Tanks trail. The ten sport routes are all on the hard side: six in the 5.11 range and four at 5.12, so this is a spot for climbers who are already warmed up and climbing at a solid level, not a beginner crag. The left side of the wall faces southeast and the right side faces southwest, which means it collects sun for much of the day. Like everywhere in Red Rock, the sandstone is fragile after rain.

nv_boulder_b_bat_cave.blurb: A pair of cave boulders within the Washoe Boulders, in the Carson City area of western Nevada. Boulder B is the eastern cave, and you can walk straight through it; the Bat Cave is the smaller of the two. The ten problems run from very easy up to V4, with most falling between V2 and V4, and the cave lines are steep and sometimes punishing on the skin. The wider Washoe area can be visited year-round, though summer gets hot, and it is a good place to pair with the nearby classic boulders in the same cluster.
